n: The problem isn’t God. His arm isn’t too short to save, nor His ear too dull to hear.

f.w: the LORD's hand is not shortened

n: It’s our sins that have built a wall between us and God and hidden His face. Sin causes separation; the Atonement of Christ is what bridges it.

f.w: your iniquities have separated between you and your God

n: Their hands are stained with blood, their fingers with wrongdoing; their lips lie and mutter wickedness.

f.w: your hands are defiled with blood

n: No one sues for justice or argues honestly in court. They trust empty words, plot trouble, and give birth to evil.

f.w: they conceive mischief

n: Their schemes are like hatching viper eggs or weaving spider webs: eat the eggs and you die; crack one and a snake comes out.

f.w: cockatrice
f.g: An old word for a venomous snake, probably a viper.

n: Spider webs make useless clothing—their deeds can’t cover them. Their hands are full of violence.
Their feet rush to do evil and shed innocent blood; ruin follows them wherever they go. Paul quotes this in describing universal sinfulness.

f.w: Their feet run to evil

n: They don’t know the way of peace; there is no justice in their paths, and anyone who follows them won’t find peace.

f.w: The way of peace they know not

n: Now the people confess: that is why justice is far from us. We wait for light but see only darkness.

f.w: we wait for light, but behold obscurity
obscurity

n: We feel our way along the wall like blind people, stumbling at noon as if it were night. Among the living we are like the dead.

f.w: We grope for the wall like the blind

n: We growl like bears and moan like doves, longing for justice and salvation that never come.

f.w: mourn sore like doves

n: An honest confession: our sins are many and testify against us; we know them well. Recognizing sin is the first step of repentance.

f.w: our sins testify against us

n: We rebelled, denied the Lord, turned from God, spoke oppression and revolt, and muttered lies from the heart.

f.w: departing away from our God

n: Justice is pushed back, righteousness stands far off, truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty can’t get in.

f.w: truth is fallen in the street
f.g: The street or town square was where courts met; truth has collapsed in public life.

f.w: equity

n: Truth is missing, and anyone who turns from evil becomes a target. The Lord saw this and was displeased that there was no justice.

f.w: he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey

n: God saw no one to step in and was amazed that no one would intervene. So His own arm brought salvation. Latter-day Saints see Christ as the One who came when no one else could save.

f.w: wondered that there was no intercessor
his arm brought salvation unto him

n: The Lord dresses for battle: righteousness as a breastplate, salvation as a helmet, vengeance as clothing, and zeal as a cloak. Paul borrows this armor for the believer.

f.w: he put on righteousness as a breastplate

n: He will repay people according to their deeds—wrath to His enemies, even to distant lands.

f.w: According to their deeds
recompence

n: From west to east people will fear His name. When the enemy rushes in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord will raise a banner against him.

f.w: When the enemy shall come in like a flood
f.g: Many translators read: “He will come like a rushing river driven by the wind (Spirit) of the Lord.”

f.w: a standard

n: A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from sin. Paul quotes this as fulfilled in Christ, who will save Israel.

f.w: the Redeemer shall come to Zion
them that turn from transgression

n: God’s covenant: His Spirit and His words will stay in His people’s mouths and their descendants’ forever. Latter-day Saints see this in continuing revelation and in parents teaching children the gospel.

f.w: this is my covenant with them
my words which I have put in thy mouth
